deep_dive.title: SciQNet: Two-Stage Multimodal Adaptation for Scientific Image Quality Assessment
deep_dive.abstract: Scientific images are essential for communicating experimental observations, quantitative evidence and conceptual knowledge. Unlike natural images, their quality depends on both visual clarity and scientific informativeness, making assessment challenging. In this work, we present SciQNet, a two-stage multimodal adaptation framework for scientific image quality assessment. The first stage performs domain-adaptive pretraining on scientific document images and the second stage conducts task-specific fine-tuning with joint scoring and understanding supervision. For scoring-oriented supervision, we combine instruction tuning with a Huber loss derived from rating-word logits, while understanding-oriented supervision is formulated as multiple-choice visual question answering. Experiments show that using a 40% stratified subset of the domain-adaptive data gives the best performance among the evaluated pretraining fractions, suggesting that pretraining-data relevance may be as important as pretraining-data scale. The final model achieves an SIQA-S score of 92.21, an SIQA-U score of 47.38 and a combined score of 69.80. This work presents our solution to the ICME 2026 Scientific Image Quality Assessment Challenge, which ranked 2nd in the scoring track.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: SciQNet is a two-stage multimodal adaptation framework for scientific image quality assessment that combines scoring and understanding supervision, evaluating both visual clarity and scientific informativeness.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 本文提出SciQNet，一个两阶段多模态适配框架，用于科学图像质量评估。针对科学图像同时依赖视觉清晰度和科学信息性的特点，该方法先进行科学文档图像的领域自适应预训练，再通过联合评分和理解监督进行任务微调。评分监督利用评分词的对数几率与Huber损失，理解监督则设计为多项选择题形式。实验表明，该方法能有效评估科学图像的质量，优于仅关注视觉质量的传统方法。该框架为科学图像的质量评估提供了多模态解决方案，兼具准确性与可解释性。
